## What you will learn

- Navigate the single Linux directory tree and say what lives in `/etc`, `/opt`, `/usr`, `/var`, `/home`, `/tmp`, `/dev`, `/proc` and `/sys`.
- Find the robotics-relevant places: `/opt/ros/jazzy`, `/dev/ttyACM0`, `/dev/serial/by-id/`, `/dev/video0`, `/dev/i2c-1`, `/etc/udev/rules.d`, `~/.ros/log`, `/boot/firmware/config.txt`.
- Explain "everything is a file": read CPU temperature from `/sys`, identify a device file with `ls -l`.
- Create and debug symbolic links, including dangling ones.
- Read mounts with `df`, `lsblk` and `findmnt`, and know what `/mnt/c` in WSL is.

## Why it matters

The robot's hardware appears to your programs as **files**. The Pico is `/dev/ttyACM0`
([01.05](../../01-first-robot/01.05-pico-microcontroller-setup.md)), the USB webcam is `/dev/video0`
([07.08 RGB cameras](../../07-sensors/07.08-rgb-cameras.md)), the IMU sits behind `/dev/i2c-1`. ROS 2 is installed in
`/opt/ros/jazzy` ([04.02](../../04-ros2/04.02-installing-ros2.md)), its logs pile up in `~/.ros/log`, and a
service that starts the robot lives in `/etc/systemd/system` ([FL.06](FL.06-processes-systemd.md)).
When a driver says "could not open port" or a launch file "cannot find package", you need to know where to look.
The next lesson, [FL.05](FL.05-permissions-users-groups.md), adds *who* is allowed to open those files.

## Concept

### One tree, no drive letters

Windows has a forest: `C:\`, `D:\`, `\\server\share`. Linux has **one tree** starting at `/`. Other disks, USB sticks,
SD cards, network shares and even the Windows drive under WSL are **mounted** onto a directory somewhere in that
tree. A USB stick doesn't become `E:`, it becomes `/media/you/STICK`. In WSL, your `C:` drive is `/mnt/c`.

### Everything is a file (almost)

Linux exposes most things through the filesystem API: open, read, write, close.

- A **regular file**: your code, a YAML config.
- A **directory**.
- A **device file** in `/dev`: reading `/dev/ttyACM0` reads bytes from the Pico over USB, and writing sends bytes.
  The same `open()`/`read()` you'd use for a text file, plus some serial settings.
- A **virtual file** in `/proc` and `/sys`: no disk behind it. The kernel generates the content when you read.
  `cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp` asks the kernel for the CPU temperature right now.
- A **symbolic link**: a small file that points to another path, like a Windows shortcut but transparent to programs.

For a .NET developer: think of `/dev` and `/sys` as a huge, standardized `Stream` API to the hardware and kernel.
The same code that tails a log file can talk to a serial port.

> [!TIP]
> **Ask your teacher:** "Show me how opening /dev/ttyACM0 in Python ends up as bytes on the Pico's USB CDC endpoint. Which layers are in between?"

## Technical explanation

### Level 1 — The map (Filesystem Hierarchy Standard)

| Path | What lives there | Robotics example |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | root of the tree | — |
| `/home/<user>` (`~`) | your files, dotfile configs | `~/karmel_ws`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.ros/log` |
| `/root` | the root user's home | rarely used directly |
| `/etc` | system-wide **configuration** (text files) | `/etc/udev/rules.d/`, `/etc/systemd/system/`, `/etc/netplan/`, `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/` |
| `/opt` | self-contained add-on software | **`/opt/ros/jazzy`** |
| `/usr/bin`, `/usr/lib` | programs and libraries installed by apt | `/usr/bin/python3`, `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages` |
| `/usr/local` | software you install by hand (not apt) | a locally built library |
| `/var` | variable data: logs, caches, spools | `/var/log/`, `/var/lib/apt/lists` |
| `/tmp` | temporary files, cleared at reboot | build scratch |
| `/dev` | device files | `/dev/ttyACM0`, `/dev/video0`, `/dev/i2c-1`, `/dev/gpiochip0`, `/dev/shm` |
| `/proc` | virtual: processes and kernel info | `/proc/cpuinfo`, `/proc/loadavg`, `/proc/<pid>/` |
| `/sys` | virtual: devices, drivers, kernel knobs | `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp` |
| `/run` | runtime state (tmpfs), since boot | PID files, sockets, `/run/user/1000` |
| `/boot` | kernel and bootloader | on Ubuntu for Raspberry Pi: `/boot/firmware/config.txt` |
| `/media`, `/mnt` | mount points for removable / manual mounts | SD card reader, WSL's `/mnt/c` |

On Ubuntu 24.04, `/bin`, `/sbin` and `/lib` are symlinks into `/usr` (`/bin -> usr/bin`). This is a historical
merge, and both paths work.

### Level 2 — Robot-specific files in detail

**`/opt/ros/jazzy`** contains `bin/` (the `ros2` CLI), `lib/` (C++ libraries, Python packages under
`lib/python3.12/site-packages`), `share/` (package manifests, launch files, message definitions), and `setup.bash`.
Nothing here is on your `PATH` until you `source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash` ([FL.03](FL.03-shell-basics.md)).
Never edit files under `/opt/ros`. apt owns them and will overwrite your changes.

**Serial devices:**

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `/dev/ttyACM0`, `ttyACM1`… | USB **CDC-ACM** devices: boards that speak USB serial natively, such as the Raspberry Pi Pico running MicroPython or an Arduino Uno R4 |
| `/dev/ttyUSB0`… | USB-to-serial **converter chips** (CH340, CP2102, FTDI): many LiDARs and cheap boards |
| `/dev/ttyAMA0`, `/dev/serial0` | the Pi's own UART on the GPIO header |
| `/dev/serial/by-id/usb-…` | **stable symlinks** named after the USB device's vendor, product and serial number |

The number (`0`, `1`) is assigned **in plug-in order**. Plug the LiDAR in before the Pico and the Pico becomes
`ttyACM1`. Your config should therefore use the stable path, e.g.
`/dev/serial/by-id/usb-MicroPython_Board_in_FS_mode_e6614c311b7e6f35-if00 -> ../../ttyACM0`, or a udev rule that
creates your own name ([FL.05](FL.05-permissions-users-groups.md), [03.03](../../03-robot-software/03.03-robust-serial-communication.md)).

**Cameras:** a USB webcam typically creates **two** nodes, `/dev/video0` (the image stream) and `/dev/video1`
(metadata). If a driver opens `video1` you get "no image". `v4l2-ctl --list-devices` (package `v4l-utils`) shows
which is which. `/dev/v4l/by-id/` gives stable names, like serial.

**Buses and pins (on the Pi):** `/dev/i2c-1` (the I2C bus on header pins 3/5), `/dev/spidev0.0`,
`/dev/gpiochip*` (GPIO via libgpiod / lgpio).

**`/dev/shm`**: shared memory. ROS 2's default DDS (Fast DDS) puts shared-memory segments here for processes
on the same machine. This matters when two Docker containers try to talk ([FL.12](FL.12-docker-for-robotics.md)).

**Logs:** `~/.ros/log/` fills with one directory per `ros2 launch`/`ros2 run`. On a Pi with a 32 GB SD card, check it
now and then (`du -sh ~/.ros/log`). System service logs live in the journal (`journalctl`, [FL.06](FL.06-processes-systemd.md)).

### Level 3 — Reading device files with `ls -l`

```text
crw-rw---- 1 root dialout 166, 0 Sep 16 10:12 /dev/ttyACM0
│└┬┘└┬┘└┬┘   └┬─┘ └──┬──┘ └──┬─┘
│ │  │  │     │      │       └ major, minor device numbers (166 = ttyACM driver, minor 0 = first one)
│ │  │  │     │      └ group that owns it (members may read/write: see FL.05)
│ │  │  │     └ owner
│ └──┴──┴ permissions for owner / group / others
└ type: c = character device, b = block device (disk), d = directory, l = symlink, - = regular file
```

A character device has a **size** replaced by `major, minor` numbers. The major number selects the kernel driver
(`1` = memory devices like `/dev/null`, `166` = USB ACM serial, `81` = video4linux). Verified on Ubuntu 24.04:
`ls -l /dev/null` shows `crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 1, 3 … /dev/null`.

**Virtual files in numbers.** `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp` returns **millidegrees Celsius** as an integer:

$$
T_{\text{°C}} = \frac{\text{value}}{1000}
$$

If it reads `52312`, then $T = 52312 / 1000 = 52.312$ °C. The Raspberry Pi 5 starts throttling its CPU at around 80–85 °C,
so a `ros2 launch` on a Pi without a cooler shows up in this file long before it shows up as a "slow SLAM" mystery.

### Level 4 — Paths, links and mounts

- **Absolute** paths start with `/` (`/opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash`). **Relative** paths start from the current directory
  (`config/karmel.yaml`). `.` is here, `..` is the parent, `~` is your home (expanded by the shell, so not inside quotes).
- **Symbolic link**: `ln -s TARGET LINKNAME`. A relative target is resolved **relative to the link's own directory**,
  not to where you ran `ln`. If the target moves, the link **dangles** and opening it fails with
  `No such file or directory` even though `ls` shows the link. `readlink LINK` shows the stored target, and
  `readlink -f LINK` resolves it to a full path.
- **Hard link** (`ln` without `-s`): a second name for the same data on the same filesystem. It is rarely what you want for configs.
- **Mounts**: `df -h` shows mounted filesystems and free space, `lsblk` shows disks and partitions (the SD card
  in a reader shows as `/dev/sdb` or `/dev/mmcblk0` with partitions `…p1`, `…p2`), and `findmnt /` shows what is mounted at `/`.
  Ubuntu Desktop auto-mounts USB media under `/media/$USER/`. In WSL, `/mnt/c` is the Windows drive
  (slow for builds, [FL.02](FL.02-installing-ubuntu.md)).

## Diagram

```text
/
├── home/you/                     ← ~   (your files, dotfiles)
│   ├── karmel_ws/src, build, install, log
│   ├── .ros/log/                 ← ROS 2 run logs (grows!)
│   └── .ssh/                     ← keys (FL.08)
├── etc/                          ← configuration (text)
│   ├── udev/rules.d/99-karmel.rules   (FL.05)
│   ├── systemd/system/karmel-bringup.service (FL.06)
│   ├── apt/sources.list.d/ros2.sources (FL.07)
│   └── netplan/*.yaml            (network, FL.09)
├── opt/ros/jazzy/                ← ROS 2 (bin, lib, share, setup.bash) — owned by apt
├── usr/bin, usr/lib              ← apt-installed programs, system Python 3.12
├── var/log/                      ← system logs
├── dev/                          ← devices (created by the kernel + udev)
│   ├── ttyACM0      c 166,0  ← Pico (USB CDC)
│   ├── serial/by-id/usb-MicroPython_Board_in_FS_mode_…-if00 → ../../ttyACM0
│   ├── video0       c 81,0   ← USB webcam stream   (video1 = metadata)
│   ├── i2c-1, gpiochip*      ← Pi header buses / pins
│   └── shm/                  ← shared memory (Fast DDS)
├── proc/  sys/                   ← virtual: kernel & hardware state (temperature, load)
├── boot/firmware/config.txt      ← Raspberry Pi firmware settings (Ubuntu on Pi)
└── mnt/c                         ← Windows C: drive (WSL only)
```

## Code

A hardware inventory script. Run it on the laptop, in WSL, in Docker, and on the Pi with the Pico plugged in.
`shopt -s nullglob` makes an unmatched glob like `/dev/ttyACM*` expand to nothing instead of the literal text.

`~/bin/robot-inventory.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# robot-inventory.sh — what hardware-facing files does this Linux machine expose?
set -uo pipefail
shopt -s nullglob          # a glob that matches nothing expands to nothing (not to itself)

section() { printf '\n[%s]\n' "$1"; }

section "serial ports"
ports=(/dev/ttyACM* /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyAMA*)
if (( ${#ports[@]} == 0 )); then echo "  none"; fi
for p in "${ports[@]}"; do ls -l "$p" | awk '{print "  " $1, $3, $4, $NF}'; done
for link in /dev/serial/by-id/*; do
  printf '  %s -> %s\n' "$(basename "$link")" "$(readlink -f "$link")"
done

section "cameras (V4L2)"
cams=(/dev/video*)
if (( ${#cams[@]} == 0 )); then echo "  none"; fi
for c in "${cams[@]}"; do ls -l "$c" | awk '{print "  " $1, $3, $4, $NF}'; done

section "I2C buses and GPIO chips"
buses=(/dev/i2c-* /dev/gpiochip*)
if (( ${#buses[@]} == 0 )); then echo "  none"; fi
for b in "${buses[@]}"; do ls -l "$b" | awk '{print "  " $1, $3, $4, $NF}'; done

section "system"
for z in /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp; do
  milli=$(<"$z")
  printf '  %s: %d.%d C\n' "$(basename "$(dirname "$z")")" $((milli / 1000)) $((milli % 1000 / 100))
done
printf '  load average (1/5/15 min): %s\n' "$(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg)"
printf '  memory available: %s MB\n' $(( $(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print $2}' /proc/meminfo) / 1024 ))
df -h / | awk 'NR==2 {print "  root filesystem: " $3 " used of " $2 " (" $5 ")"}'
if [[ -d /opt/ros ]]; then printf '  ROS installs: %s\n' "$(ls /opt/ros | tr '\n' ' ')"; else echo "  ROS installs: none in /opt/ros"; fi
if [[ -d "$HOME/.ros/log" ]]; then printf '  ROS logs: %s\n' "$(du -sh "$HOME/.ros/log" | cut -f1)"; fi
```

Run: `bash ~/bin/robot-inventory.sh`.

### Exercise FL.04-E1 — Tour the tree `[coding]`

1. `ls /` and `ls -l /bin /lib`
2. `ls -l /dev/null /dev/zero /dev/urandom` and `stat -c '%F' /dev/null /etc /etc/hostname`

5. `df -h /` and `findmnt -n -o TARGET,FSTYPE /`

### Exercise FL.04-E2 — Break a symlink on purpose `[predict]`

Hardware: none. Predict the output of each `cat` and `ls -l` before running:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/robot/config && cd ~/robot
echo "wheel_radius: 0.033" > config/karmel_v1.yaml
ln -s config/karmel_v1.yaml active.yaml
ls -l active.yaml; cat active.yaml
readlink active.yaml; readlink -f active.yaml
mv config config_old
cat active.yaml; echo "exit=$?"
ls -l active.yaml
mv config_old config
```

2. Run it in `ros:jazzy-ros-base` (`docker run --rm -it -v "${PWD}:/s" ros:jazzy-ros-base bash /s/robot-inventory.sh`).

### Exercise FL.04-E4 — Kernel numbers to physical units `[numerical]`

Hardware: none.

1. `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp` reads `78950`. What temperature is it, and should you worry on a Pi 5?
2. `/proc/meminfo` says `MemAvailable: 1843200 kB`. How many MB is that (1 MB = 1024 kB)?
3. `df -h /` on the Pi says `Size 29G, Used 22G`. `du -sh ~/.ros/log` says `3.1G`. What percentage of the used space is ROS logs?

## Expected result

**FL.04-E1:** `ls /` lists `bin boot dev etc home lib … opt proc root run sbin srv sys tmp usr var`.
`ls -l /bin /lib` shows `lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 7 … /bin -> usr/bin` and `/lib -> usr/lib`. Device files:

```text
crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 1, 3 Sep 16 20:09 /dev/null
crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 1, 9 Sep 16 20:09 /dev/urandom
crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 1, 5 Sep 16 20:09 /dev/zero
```

`stat` prints `character special file`, `directory`, `regular file`. `readlink -f /bin/sh` prints `/usr/bin/dash`
(Ubuntu's `sh` is dash, not bash). In Docker, `findmnt` prints `/      overlay`. On a real install it's `ext4`.

**FL.04-E2:**

```text
lrwxrwxrwx 1 you you 21 Sep 16 20:09 active.yaml -> config/karmel_v1.yaml
wheel_radius: 0.033
config/karmel_v1.yaml
/home/you/robot/config/karmel_v1.yaml
cat: active.yaml: No such file or directory
exit=1
lrwxrwxrwx 1 you you 21 Sep 16 20:09 active.yaml -> config/karmel_v1.yaml
```

The link itself still exists, has the same size (21 = length of the target string) and still points to the same text.
Only the target is missing. On a color terminal `ls` shows the dangling link in red. After moving `config` back, `cat` works again.

**FL.04-E3:** In `ubuntu:24.04` every hardware section says `none`, followed by load, memory, root filesystem and
`ROS installs: none in /opt/ros` (no thermal line: containers on Docker Desktop don't expose a thermal zone). In
`ros:jazzy-ros-base` the last line becomes `ROS installs: jazzy`. On the Pi with the Pico plugged in:

```text
[serial ports]
  crw-rw---- root dialout /dev/ttyACM0
  usb-MicroPython_Board_in_FS_mode_<serial>-if00 -> /dev/ttyACM0
```

plus `/dev/i2c-*` and `/dev/gpiochip*` entries and a `thermal_zone0: 4x.x C` line. Unplugged: `/dev/ttyACM0` and its
by-id link disappear, because udev removes device files when the device goes away.

**FL.04-E4:** (1) $78950/1000 = 78.95$ °C. That's close to the Pi 5's throttling range (~80–85 °C). Add the active
cooler before running SLAM. (2) $1843200 / 1024 = 1800$ MB. (3) $3.1 / 22 \approx 0.141$, so **14 %** of used space is
old ROS logs. Clean them with `rm -rf ~/.ros/log/*` when nothing is running.

## Troubleshooting

### Symptom: "could not open port /dev/ttyACM0: No such file or directory"

1. `ls /dev/ttyACM* /dev/ttyUSB*`: does any serial device exist? If not, check the cable (charge-only USB cables are common),
   then `sudo dmesg | tail -20` right after plugging in. You should see `cdc_acm … ttyACM0: USB ACM device`.
2. It exists but as `ttyACM1`: another device took `0`. Use `/dev/serial/by-id/…` in your config.
3. In WSL: the device must be attached with `usbipd` first ([FL.02](FL.02-installing-ubuntu.md)).
4. In Docker: the device must be passed with `--device` ([FL.12](FL.12-docker-for-robotics.md)).
5. If the error is `Permission denied` instead, go to [FL.05](FL.05-permissions-users-groups.md).

### Symptom: a config or launch file "doesn't exist" but you can see it

1. Relative path? Programs resolve relative paths from **their** working directory, not the file's location. Print
   `pwd` in the same context, or use an absolute path / `ament_index` package share path in ROS.
2. `ls -l` shows an arrow? Then `readlink -f` it. It may be a dangling symlink.
3. Case: `Karmel.yaml` vs `karmel.yaml`.
4. A trailing `\r` in a path read from a Windows-edited file: `cat -A pathlist.txt`.

### Symptom: the disk is full on the Pi

`df -h` → which filesystem? Then run `du -sh ~/.ros/log ~/karmel_ws/build ~/karmel_ws/log /var/log 2>/dev/null` and
`sudo journalctl --disk-usage`. The usual culprits, in order: ROS logs, rosbags, colcon `build/`, Docker images
(`docker system df`), the journal.

## Common mistakes

- **Hard-coding `/dev/ttyACM0`**: it changes with plug order. Use `/dev/serial/by-id/` or a udev symlink.
- **Editing files under `/opt/ros` or `/usr`**: apt owns them and the next upgrade reverts your change. Override in your workspace or `/etc` instead.
- **Opening `/dev/video1` for a webcam** that uses `video0` for frames and `video1` for metadata.
- **Creating symlinks with the wrong relative base**: a relative target is resolved from the link's directory.
- **Putting the ROS workspace under `/mnt/c` in WSL.**
- **Forgetting that `/tmp` is wiped at reboot**: don't keep calibration results there.
- **Assuming `sh` is bash**: on Ubuntu it's dash.

## Knowledge check

1. Where are the ROS 2 Jazzy binaries installed, and why aren't they on your `PATH` by default?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   `/opt/ros/jazzy` (with `bin/`, `lib/`, `share/`, `setup.bash`). `/opt` is for self-contained add-on software that
   doesn't install into `/usr/bin`, so you opt in per terminal with `source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash`.
   </details>

2. What's the difference between `/dev/ttyACM0` and `/dev/ttyUSB0`?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   `ttyACM*` are USB CDC-ACM devices, boards that implement USB serial themselves (the Pico with MicroPython).
   `ttyUSB*` are USB-to-UART converter chips (CH340, CP2102, FTDI) with their own kernel drivers.
   </details>

3. `ls -l` shows `crw-rw---- 1 root video 81, 0 … /dev/video0`. What do `c`, `video` and `81, 0` mean?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   `c` = character device. `video` = the owning group, whose members may read/write. `81, 0` = major number 81
   (the video4linux driver) and minor 0 (the first such device). There is no size for device files.
   </details>

4. After a reboot your LiDAR is `/dev/ttyUSB0` and your motor board `/dev/ttyUSB1`. Yesterday it was the other way
   around. What's the robust fix?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   Don't use numbered names. Use `/dev/serial/by-id/usb-…` in configs, or a udev rule that matches vendor/product/serial
   and creates a fixed symlink like `/dev/karmel_lidar` (FL.05, 03.03).
   </details>

5. `cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp` prints `61234`. Temperature? Where is this "file" stored on disk?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   61.234 °C (millidegrees). It isn't stored anywhere: `/sys` is a virtual filesystem, and the kernel produces the value when you read.
   </details>

6. You created `ln -s karmel.yaml ~/robot/config/active.yaml` while standing in `~/robot`, where `karmel.yaml` lives.
   `cat ~/robot/config/active.yaml` fails. Why?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   A relative symlink target is resolved relative to the **link's directory** (`~/robot/config/`), where there's no
   `karmel.yaml`. Use `ln -s ../karmel.yaml config/active.yaml` or an absolute target.
   </details>

7. In WSL, where is `C:\Users\you\Downloads`, and why shouldn't your workspace live there?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>

   `/mnt/c/Users/you/Downloads`. It's the Windows filesystem mounted through a cross-OS file protocol: much slower for
   builds, and Linux permissions don't map cleanly.
   </details>

## Practical challenge

Make the robot's serial device name independent of plug order *without* udev (that's FL.05):

- Write `find-pico.sh` that prints the **stable** path for the Pico by looking through `/dev/serial/by-id/` for a name
  containing `MicroPython`, and exits with code 1 and a clear message on stderr if none is found or more than one is found.
- Use it in a one-liner that opens a serial terminal: `python3 -m serial.tools.miniterm "$(find-pico.sh)" 115200`
  (package `python3-serial`).
- Test all three cases: no Pico, one Pico, and "two" Picos. Without hardware, create a fake directory tree
  with symlinks and pass its location as an optional argument (default `/dev/serial/by-id`).

Acceptance criteria: correct output and exit code in all three cases, no numbered `ttyACM` path in the output, and
`shellcheck find-pico.sh` reports nothing.

## Go deeper

- https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/FHS_3.0/fhs/index.html — the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard 3.0, the official "what goes where".
- https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/devices.html — the kernel's list of device major/minor numbers.
- https://linuxcommand.org/tlcl.php — *The Linux Command Line*, chapters on navigation, exploring the system and links.
- https://missing.csail.mit.edu/ — Missing Semester, "Course overview + the shell" for navigating the tree efficiently.
- https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/filesystems/sysfs.html — how `/sys` works, when you want to read hardware state from code.

## Progress checkpoint

- [ ] I can say what lives in `/etc`, `/opt`, `/usr`, `/var`, `/dev`, `/proc` and `/sys`.
- [ ] I can find the Pico, a webcam and the ROS installation on disk, and read their `ls -l` lines.
- [ ] I can create, inspect and fix symbolic links.
- [ ] I can check disk space and mounts and find what is filling a disk.
